summary: Tested iteration 12's webhook migration (replacing long-polling). Verified full activate flow end-to-end on backend + frontend: GET /api/bot/status new fields (is_live_here/webhook_active, polling_enabled correctly removed), POST /api/admin/telegram/activate (401 without auth, 200 with correct webhook_url/pending_update_count on success), POST /api/telegram/webhook/{secret} auth boundary (404 for wrong path secret, missing header, wrong header; 200 with both correct), and regressions (/api/r bridge 302, GET/PUT /api/settings auth-gating, POST /api/admin/broadcast sent>0). Frontend: reloaded dashboard while locked -> amber '[ not live here ]' pill shown correctly (webhook had been deleted beforehand to start from the documented clean state), terminal header shows 'transport ... webhook' (no 'long-poll' text found), unlocked with PIN 246810, activate-webhook-btn appeared, clicked it, activate-webhook-status showed 'this environment is now live', and bot-status-pill flipped to green '[ system online ]' after loadStatus() refresh -- conversions/unique-users counters also ticked up live confirming real webhook traffic was being received during the test.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py bot_status(): correctly derives own_base from x-forwarded-host/host header and compares webhook_url.startswith(own_base) to compute is_live_here -- this correctly avoids relying on any .env value, matching the stated architecture goal.

activate_telegram endpoint correctly derives base_url from the incoming request's Host header (not .env), so it will always activate whichever environment (preview vs production) the admin is actually browsing -- verified webhook_url returned matched the preview domain exactly.

telegram_webhook endpoint double-checks the secret in both the URL path AND the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header before processing -- good defense in depth; both checks independently verified to 404 on mismatch.

bot.py init_bot() is called unconditionally at startup with no start_polling call, confirming the 'safe in every environment' claim -- no risk of the previous env-var-scoping bug recurring since there's no polling flag to sync incorrectly.

Minor observation (not a bug): GET /api/bot/status makes a live get_webhook_info() Telegram API call on every request (no caching) -- fine at current traffic but could be cached for a few seconds if this endpoint is polled by many dashboard tabs simultaneously.
seed_data_creation: None persisted beyond expected test side-effects: one harmless webhook update (fake message) sent to the /api/telegram/webhook/{secret} auth-success test, and one broadcast message 'testing broadcast still works after webhook migration' sent to real test users (per instructions, expected).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 12 (Telegram long-polling -> webhook migration) fully verified end-to-end, no bugs found. Final state left after testing: preview's webhook IS currently activated and pointing at the preview domain (is_live_here:true, webhook_active:true, online:true) as a natural result of running the activation flow test -- per instructions this does not need to be cleaned up/deleted; main agent will separately instruct the user to activate from the PRODUCTION dashboard as the real final step (production is untouched/untested by this agent, out of scope). If a future iteration wants to test the deactivated starting state again, first call Telegram's deleteWebhook API (bot token in backend/.env) before reloading the frontend.
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs found in this iteration's scope; this was a verification pass of the fix for the prior BOT_POLLING_ENABLED production outage bug, and the new webhook-based design (deriving public URL from request Host header rather than .env) was confirmed to correctly avoid that class of bug.
